::: {#exm-all-horses}
#### A proof by induction that fails

Claim (false): in every group of $n \ge 1$ horses, all the horses are the same color.

"Proof":

- **Base case.**
  A group of 1 horse has only one color.
- **Inductive step.**
  Suppose every group of $k$ horses is all one color,
  and take a group of $k + 1$ horses.
  Leaving out the first horse leaves $k$ horses, which are all one color,
  and leaving out the last horse leaves $k$ horses, which are all one color.
  The horses in the middle are in both groups,
  so the two colors are the same, and all $k + 1$ horses are one color.

The inductive step fails for $k = 1$:
a group of 2 horses splits into two groups of 1 horse with no horse in both,
so nothing links the two colors.
So $P(1)$ does not imply $P(2)$, and the chain of implications breaks at its first link.
An inductive step has to work for *every* $k \ge n_0$, including the smallest.

:::
